gen-fs-quilon-gf-parkinsans: Parkinsans keeps every stroke one thickness, a crisp plain sans whose wide-mouthed letters hold up even when small. Quilon swells and thins gently like a dip pen, which is where its pull lies.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-pathway-extreme: Crisp and compact, with Quilon leading in a restrained editorial voice. Pathway Extreme follows with a big x-height and stubby ascenders, so a long passage feels sturdy and easy to move through.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-preahvihear: Preahvihear has a lofty x-height and letter mouths pried open like an oyster shell, set beneath Quilon's commanding display look. Preahvihear keeps its strokes low in contrast, so a long passage moves along smoothly under the heading's gentle thick-thin shifts.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-prompt: Prompt reads oversized in its small letters, with open apertures that make a plain sans feel approachable and quick to take in. Prompt stays low in contrast under Quilon's subtle modulation, so the editorial heading gets all the drama.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-pt-sans-caption: Quilon brings a commanding editorial voice with slight thinning at the sides of its bowls. PT Sans Caption answers with big-bodied lowercase and unclosed, inviting bowls, so the two sit together like a firm headline over a friendly, low-contrast voice.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-puritan: Approachable and clean, Puritan has rounded forms that stay open to the side and oversized counters in its e and a. Puritan's low contrast sits comfortably under Quilon, whose thick and thin strokes are close enough to feel related.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-questrial: Questrial cuts its letters flat and stencil-like, every stroke carrying the same visual weight in a tall band over short stalks, a plain sans through and through. Quilon earns its keep big and short.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-radio-canada: Radio Canada draws tall, full lowercase with the steadiness of a technical pen, a plain sans with a clear opening at every curve. And Quilon does the opposite job best, giving big lines a soft, restrained thick-thin ratio.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-radio-canada-big: Quilon sets an editorial, commanding tone with bowls that shift gently in weight. Radio Canada Big is the steadying counterpart: a monoline skeleton, an x-height filling the line, and terminals finishing well clear of the stem.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-readex-pro: Readex Pro holds every stroke at one gauge, with broad terminal gaps and a tiny step from lowercase to caps. Quilon is the one to enjoy for its modest weight shift inside each stroke, while the body simply keeps going.
